name: China Masters
stakes: This week at the China Masters is vital for India's top shuttlers to build momentum and consolidate their rankings in the post-World Championships landscape, especially with the Asian Games on the horizon.
summary:
India's badminton contingent steps onto the courts at the China Masters, a crucial Super 750 event following the World Championships. Men's Doubles fifth seeds Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty will be looking to push past their Worlds quarterfinal exit, though lingering fitness concerns remain a watchpoint. Meanwhile, PV Sindhu, ranked 10th, aims for a strong rebound after her R16 departure in Copenhagen, seeking to regain her formidable touch.

Lakshya Sen, spearheading the Men's Singles challenge, enters the tournament seeking a deeper run after his own early Worlds exit. The spotlight also shines on the Women's Doubles pair of Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand, who arrive in Shenzhen riding high on their historic World Championships bronze medal—a performance that signals their top form and rising stature. While the draw cards are still taking shape for many, the early rounds have already seen some Indian hopefuls exit the competition, underscoring the tough challenges ahead.
